name: Quandary Peak
line_notes: High-volume warmup line; Cristo is a direct E couloir off Blue Lakes.

name: Mt. Lincoln
line_notes: Part of the DeCaLiBron loop; NE amphitheater lines.

name: Mt. Bross
line_notes: Bross summit access is private in summer; spring snow eases that. Low angle.

name: Mt. Democrat
line_notes: Steepest of the DeCaLiBron group.

name: Mt. Sherman
line_notes: Mellow, wind-scoured; coverage (not angle) is the usual problem.

name: Grays Peak
line_notes: Grays/Torreys linkup from Stevens Gulch.

name: Torreys Peak
line_notes: Dead Dog is the classic; linkup with Grays.

name: Mt. Bierstadt
line_notes: Sawtooth/NE couloirs; West Slopes are the gentle fallback.

name: Mt. Blue Sky
line_notes: Formerly Mt. Evans. Long approach with Mt. Evans Rd closed.

name: Longs Peak
line_notes: CRUX. Continuity to the true summit (Homestretch/Notch) is rare; very late window. Tier-2 strictness.

name: Pikes Peak
line_notes: Continuity poor; ski descents are opportunistic. Far edge of CAIC Front Range coverage.

name: Mt. Elbert
line_notes: Highest in CO; broad E faces.

name: Mt. Massive
line_notes: Big, broad; multiple summits along the ridge.

name: Mt. Harvard
line_notes: Long approach; shares TH with Columbia.

name: La Plata Peak
line_notes: N/NW lines hold cold snow late; PWL-sensitive aspects.

name: Mt. Antero
line_notes: Very long 4WD road inflates approach when gated.

name: Mt. Shavano
line_notes: Iconic snow-angel couloir; corn line. Linkup with Tabeguache.

name: Tabeguache Peak
line_notes: Reached via the Shavano saddle; strictest go/no-go governs the linkup.

name: Mt. Princeton
line_notes: Wind-hammered E slopes; coverage variable. Road walk if gated.

name: Mt. Yale
line_notes: Moderate, popular.

name: Mt. Columbia
line_notes: Often paired with Harvard from North Cottonwood; loose when thin.

name: Mt. Oxford
line_notes: Bagged via the Belford traverse; big-vert linkup day.

name: Mt. Belford
line_notes: Hub of the Missouri Gulch linkup.

name: Missouri Mountain
line_notes: Steepest of the Missouri Gulch trio; cornice-guarded.

name: Huron Peak
line_notes: Winfield road gating doubles the approach in season.

name: Mt. of the Holy Cross
line_notes: CRUX. The Cross Couloir is a committing N line; holds cold/PWL snow. Long approach with Tigiwon road gated.

name: Uncompahgre Peak
line_notes: Highest San Juan; long gated road. S/E corn aspects.

name: Wetterhorn Peak
line_notes: CRUX. Rocky summit block -- continuity to the TRUE summit is the validity crux here.

name: Mt. Sneffels
line_notes: CRUX. The Snake tops out just below the summit; fill-dependent continuity. North aspect = PWL-sensitive.

name: Handies Peak
line_notes: Easiest San Juan; American Basin corn.

name: Redcloud Peak
line_notes: Linkup with Sunshine via the connecting ridge.

name: Sunshine Peak
line_notes: Lowest CO 14er; reached over Redcloud.

name: San Luis Peak
line_notes: Remote, gentle, long. CAIC coverage is coarse out here -- expect degraded-data days.

name: Mt. Eolus
line_notes: CRUX. Chicago Basin -- train + basecamp. Catwalk to the summit is rocky; continuity crux.

name: Sunlight Peak
line_notes: CRUX. Notorious summit-block scramble -- a continuous SKI to the true summit is essentially impossible; the validity test will likely veto.

name: Windom Peak
line_notes: CRUX. The most skiable of the Chicago Basin three.

name: Mt. Wilson
line_notes: CRUX. Summit block continuity crux. (El Diente, dropped from the 54, would otherwise link here via the traverse.)

name: Wilson Peak
line_notes: Different TH (Rock of Ages) than Mt. Wilson; SW corn line.

name: Crestone Peak
line_notes: CRUX. Red Gully tops out below the true summit -- continuity/validity crux. Conglomerate rock.

name: Crestone Needle
line_notes: CRUX. Among the steepest objectives; rocky summit. Linkup with Crestone Peak governed by strictest go/no-go.

name: Kit Carson Peak
line_notes: CRUX. OB Couloir is the classic; summit continuity is the validity test.

name: Challenger Point
line_notes: Bagged with Kit Carson from Willow Lake.

name: Humboldt Peak
line_notes: The gentle option from South Colony; good acclimatization day for the Crestones cluster.

name: Blanca Peak
line_notes: CRUX. Como road is brutal; big basin day with Ellingwood/Little Bear.

name: Ellingwood Point
line_notes: Linked with Blanca from Lake Como basin.

name: Little Bear Peak
line_notes: CRUX. The Hourglass tops below the chossy true summit -- the textbook continuity/validity crux of the whole project. Strictest member of the Como basin cluster.

name: Mt. Lindsey
line_notes: CRUX-tier by aspect/consequence though shorter; Huerfano road gated.

name: Culebra Peak
line_notes: CRUX for ACCESS, not avalanche: privately owned (Cielo Vista Ranch), must pre-book a permit on a day the ranch allows it. A hard scheduling constraint independent of conditions.

name: Maroon Peak
line_notes: CRUX. Bell Cord splits the Bells; rotten Maroon Formation rock. Maroon Creek road closure adds a long approach.

name: North Maroon Peak
line_notes: CRUX. The 54-list peak kept over El Diente. Rocky summit -- continuity crux. Linked with Maroon from Maroon Lake.

name: Pyramid Peak
line_notes: CRUX. The Landry Line skis from the true summit -- one of CO's most committing descents. Needs a rare bonded-corn window.

name: Snowmass Mountain
line_notes: CRUX. Long valley approach; the namesake E face. Continuity good when filled.

name: Capitol Peak
line_notes: CRUX. The hardest objective in the project: knife-edge to a rocky summit, N aspect PWL exposure. Latest, narrowest safe window -- this peak most often sets the finish date.

name: Castle Peak
line_notes: The accessible Elk 14er; Montezuma Basin road gating drives the approach. (Conundrum, dropped from the 54, links from the same basin.)
